summary: Implements absolute capture time RTP header extension value construction, timestamp rewriting, and binary marshal/unmarshal behavior.
responsibilities: Create absolute capture time values from raw NTP timestamp data
Validate required timestamp data before rewriting or marshaling
Encode and decode 8-byte and 16-byte absolute capture time payloads

summary: Absolute capture time RTP header extension identifiers.

constants.summary: URI used to identify the WebRTC absolute capture time RTP header extension.

summary: Sentinel errors returned by absolute capture time validation and decoding.

variables.summary: Returned when required absolute capture timestamp data is missing.
Returned when marshaled absolute capture time data is shorter than the required timestamp field.

summary: Stores an absolute capture timestamp and optional estimated capture clock offset for RTP header extension payloads.

inner.summary: Optional estimated capture clock offset encoded in the extended payload form.

summary: Creates an AbsCaptureTime from raw NTP timestamp and estimated capture clock offset values.
Applies a wall-clock offset to the absolute capture timestamp and clears the estimated clock offset.
summary_step: 1. Rejects missing absolute capture timestamp data.
2. Converts the NTP timestamp to time.Time and applies the supplied offset.
3. Converts the adjusted time back to NTP time.
4. Clears the estimated capture clock offset.

summary: Encodes the absolute capture time value as an 8-byte shortened payload or 16-byte extended payload.
summary_step: 1. Rejects missing absolute capture timestamp data.
2. Uses an 8-byte payload for timestamp-only encoding and adds 8 bytes when an estimated offset is present.
3. Writes the absolute capture timestamp in big-endian order.
4. Writes the estimated capture clock offset in big-endian order when present.

summary: Decodes an absolute capture time payload into timestamp and optional estimated clock offset fields.
summary_step: 1. Rejects payloads shorter than the required 8-byte absolute capture timestamp.
2. Reads the absolute capture timestamp in big-endian order.
3. Reads the estimated capture clock offset when the payload has at least 16 bytes.
4. Leaves the estimated offset unchanged when only the shortened form is present.
